newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sets terms for Thomson-CSF sale.
newsitem.headline: France sets terms for Thomson-CSF sale.

text.p: The French government set out on Wednesday the procedure for the privatisation of defence electronics company Thomson-CSF, including minimum financial terms and conditions.

The successful bidder or group would become the majority owner by acquiring more than 50 percent of Thomson-CSF's capital and voting rights. Firms bidding must have at least five billion francs in equity capital and the same amount in turnover in professional and defence electronics, the government said in a statement.

The terms and conditions -- "cahier de charges" -- mark the government's second attempt to sell Thomson-CSF through a private sale after a first effort failed last year. The government had tried to sell it as part of the privatisation of the whole Thomson SA electronics group.
The Thomson-CSF privatisation is part of the state's aim to restructure the defence industry around a few "national champions" as a step towards wider European consolidation.
The government said on Tuesday bidders must place offers by March 28 and it hopes to pick the winner by June 30.

Engineering group Alcatel Alsthom and missiles-to-publishing conglomerate Lagardere Groupe have said they are interested in bidding. Thomson-CSF makes radars, tactical missiles, radios and integrated complex systems as a defence prime contractor.
